name: Parmit Chilana
role: Associate Professor and Ebco-Eppich Research Chair
bio: I am an Associate Professor and Ebco-Eppich Research Chair at the School of Computing Science at Simon Fraser University. My main area of research is in human-computer interaction (HCI). I co-direct the Interactive Experiences Lab at SFU. My core research in HCI focuses on inventing and deploying user-centered software help and learning techniques for feature-rich applications in a variety of domains, such as 3D modeling, education, health, and software development. In particular, I am passionate about using interdisciplinary approaches to understand and design for user diversity and empower users from all backgrounds and skills levels to use, learn, and program emerging technologies. My work has been recognized with several awards and honors, including the 2022 CS-CAN Outstanding Early Career Computer Science Researcher Award, an NSERC Discovery Accelerator Award, and Best Paper Awards at venues such as ACM CHI. Before coming to SFU, I was an Assistant Professor at the University of Waterloo. I received my PhD from the University of Washington where I co-founded AnswerDash, a venture-funded startup that commercialized my award-winning dissertation work on crowdsourced contextual help retrieval.

name: Eva Mackamul
bio: Eva is a postdoc working with Dr. Parmit Chilana on interaction and feature discoverability in human-AI interaction contexts.

name: Afra Liu
bio: Afra is a PhD student co-supervised by Dr. Parmit Chilana and Dr. Nick Vincent. Her research interests broadly focus on human–AI interaction and AI literacy.

name: Aham Gupta
bio: Aham is a Master's student supervised by Dr. Parmit Chilana. His research focuses on designing and evaluating instructor-centered AI tools that integrate into teaching workflows, thereby supporting instructors in their teaching tasks.

name: Kanak Gautam
bio: Kanak is a Master's student in Computer Science at Simon Fraser University, working with Dr. Parmit Chilana. Her research focuses on HCI and user experiences in AI-assisted creative tools, especially generative 3D modeling systems.

name: Anjali Khurana
bio: Anjali Khurana is a Ph.D. student supervised by Dr. Parmit Chilana. Her research focuses on designing and developing LLM-based assistants and copilots for software help-seeking and AR/mixed reality applications that foster effective human–AI collaboration and help users form accurate mental models of these emerging technologies. During her Ph.D., she interned with Microsoft Research's FATE Group in New York, where she explored transparency and user control in LLMs, broadening her interests to include interpretability and explainable AI.
